title: Observatory Telescope
subtitle: A slit dome, an equatorial fork and a mirror that gathers light for hours
summary: A research telescope does two things at once: it collects enough light to see faint objects, and it tracks the sky as the Earth turns. The dome shields the instrument from wind and stray light, the equatorial mount follows one axis of rotation, and the primary mirror focuses starlight onto a detector.

parts.name: Dome Base
parts.short: The rotating track under the dome
parts.detail: The dome sits on a ring of rollers. A motor turns the whole shell so the slit can follow the telescope.

parts.name: Dome Shell
parts.short: A rotating hemisphere with a slit
parts.detail: The shell protects the telescope from wind and rain. Its slit opens toward the part of the sky being observed.

parts.name: Slit Frame
parts.short: The structural edge of the opening
parts.detail: The slit frame stiffens the shell where material has been removed and carries the shutter tracks.

parts.name: Dome Shutters
parts.short: Close the slit in bad weather
parts.detail: Two shutters slide or swing together to seal the opening when the observatory is not in use.

parts.name: Pier
parts.short: A rigid column from the bedrock
parts.detail: The pier is isolated from the building floor so footsteps and wind do not shake the telescope.

parts.name: Mount Base
parts.short: Connects the pier to the mount
parts.detail: The base carries the fork and the RA drive. Its bolts allow the polar axis to be aligned.

parts.name: Fork
parts.short: Holds the telescope on both sides
parts.detail: A fork mount supports the tube at two points, which is stiffer than a single-sided mount for a heavy mirror.

parts.name: Right Ascension Axis
parts.detail: The polar axis is aligned with Earth's rotation axis. Driving it at sidereal rate keeps a star fixed in the eyepiece.

parts.name: Optical Tube
parts.detail: The tube keeps the primary and secondary mirrors separated and square to the optical axis.

parts.name: Primary Mirror
parts.detail: The large concave mirror collects light and brings it to a focus near the top of the tube.

parts.name: Secondary Spider
parts.short: Holds the secondary mirror on the axis
parts.detail: Thin vanes support the secondary mirror without blocking much light. Their diffraction spikes are visible in images.

parts.name: Secondary Mirror
parts.short: Folds the light back toward the detector
parts.detail: A small convex mirror sends the converging beam back through a hole in the primary or out to a side port.

parts.name: Counterweight
parts.short: Balances the tube around the axis
parts.detail: Weights on the opposite side of the tube reduce the torque the drive must hold.

parts.name: Drive Motors
parts.detail: Motors on both axes move the telescope and hold it steady against wind and imbalance.

parts.name: Axis Encoders
parts.detail: High-resolution encoders report the axis angle so the control system knows where the telescope is pointing.

parts.name: Control Desk
parts.detail: The desk holds the computer, focus and dome controls, and the detector readout.

parts.name: Control Screen
parts.detail: The screen displays the live image, guiding corrections and exposure status.

parts.name: Access Ladder
parts.detail: A ladder gives access for maintenance and for changing instruments at the focus.

parts.name: Nameplate
parts.detail: The plate records the aperture, focal ratio and serial number.

steps.title: The dome follows the slit
steps.body: The dome turns on its roller track so the slit lines up with the telescope. The shell blocks wind and stray light while the opening admits the sky.

steps.title: A stiff pier keeps the image still
steps.body: The telescope stands on a pier separated from the floor. Any vibration in the building would blur a long exposure, so the pier goes down to bedrock.

steps.title: One axis follows the Earth
steps.body: The polar axis is aligned with Earth's rotation. Turning it once per sidereal day cancels the apparent motion of the stars, so the detector can integrate for hours.

steps.title: Two mirrors make the image
steps.body: The concave primary gathers light; the small secondary folds it toward the detector. The tube keeps both mirrors aligned to a fraction of a wavelength.

quiz.prompt: Tap the mirror that gathers the starlight.
Tap the axis that follows Earth's rotation.
Tap the part that protects the telescope from wind and light.
Why is the telescope pier separated from the building floor?
choices: To stop footsteps and wind from shaking the telescope
To make the dome turn faster
quiz.explain: A separate pier isolates the optical path from building vibrations.

quiz.prompt: What does the secondary mirror do?
choices: Folds the focused beam toward the detector
quiz.explain: It redirects the converging beam to the instrument while keeping the tube short.
